name: Minimal Changes Only
description: Only change what was requested — no bonus refactoring, style changes, or scope creep.
content:
# Minimal Changes Only Rules

- Only modify code that is directly related to the requested task — don't touch unrelated files
- Don't rename variables, reformat code, or reorganize imports unless specifically asked to
- Don't add logging, comments, or error handling beyond what the task requires
- Don't upgrade dependencies, change configurations, or modify build settings as a side effect
- If you notice something that should be improved but isn't part of the task, mention it but don't change it
- Don't convert code style (e.g., arrow functions to named functions) unless that's the request
- Don't add TypeScript types to existing JavaScript files unless asked to migrate to TypeScript
- Keep the diff as small as possible — reviewers and future debuggers will thank you
- Don't move code between files unless the task specifically requires restructuring
- Don't add new abstractions (interfaces, base classes, utilities) unless the task creates the need
- If fixing a bug, fix that specific bug — don't preemptively fix other potential bugs you notice
- When in doubt about whether a change is in scope, ask before making it
